warnings.warning: shift(1) excludes only the immediately current row after grouping and sorting; repeated same-Games rows can still leak current outcomes. Require an athlete/team plus Games cutoff test before reuse.

The static athlete-file label is not a future first-occurrence target, and it keeps already-medaled Samoa in the at-risk cohort. Reconcile NOC medal history before computing probabilities or the expected count.
USA swimming totals sum athlete and relay-member rows rather than distinct event-NOC awards, yielding impossible medal counts. Correct the statistical grain before fitting any count model.
The same USA analysis reports beta1 as 0.0517 and 0.1912 on adjacent pages. No coefficient interpretation is reusable until one authority fit and dataset are identified.
The printed exp(0.912) does not produce the stated 21.1 percent increase; the number corresponds approximately to exp(0.1912). Preserve the typo as a warning, not as a reusable calculation.

Elasticity beta1 times NumEvents is a level elasticity, while the one-event multiplicative ratio exp(beta1) is constant in this log-link model. The paper incorrectly says one additional event has a growing relative effect.

The host coefficient is an association from a sparse country time series, not an identified causal medal increase. Require comparison groups, timing checks, pretrends, and placebos before causal wording.
The 0/1/2/3 podium coding is ordinal but is averaged and differenced as an equal-interval capability scale. Reuse requires a defensible outcome metric and sensitivity to alternative scoring.
Setting epsilon to zero assigns every current-minus-history residual to the coach. This is not causal identification and must not be presented as a measured coach contribution.
The stated USA effects 2 and 1.33 average to about 1.67, not 1.16; the second attributed year also falls outside the stated coach-tenure window. Reconcile timing and arithmetic before aggregation.

global_organization_chain: Open with a task-numbered Summary that gives each official task one method-to-result capsule, then close with stakeholder use and self-evaluation.
Use the Introduction to move from Olympic scale and cadence to participant dynamics, host advantage, and the practical audiences for medal forecasts.
Restate the required country gold and total outputs, then motivate an athlete-level intermediate representation and enumerate the forecast, first-medal, event, host, and coach branches.
Place five broad stability, roster, shock, external-factor, and data-authenticity assumptions before model construction so the reader knows the forecast world being held fixed.
For Task 1, follow the workflow athlete features -> per-sport medal/gold classifiers -> constrained event allocation -> NOC aggregation -> point and interval forecasts.

For Task 2, reuse encoding and sport probabilities, narrow to nominal zero-medal NOCs, perform without-replacement event draws, and report both country probabilities and the expected number of new medal-winning NOCs.

For Task 3, move from two sport-country case studies to a broader host regression: USA swimming supplies a positive event-count case, China table tennis supplies a nonsignificant contrast, and host status becomes a third explanatory branch.
For Task 4, define a coach decomposition, operationalize its prior-three-Games baseline, illustrate it with Lang Ping, and translate the claimed effect into three country-event recommendations.

Keep verification adjacent to the model it is meant to qualify: ROC/PR/calibration beside random forests, LOO and distribution alternatives beside Poisson, and country-case comparison beside host regression.
Return from model outputs to NOC-facing suggestions, then end with strengths, limitations, a result recap, and future data/model directions.
Place the AI Use Report after the technical paper as a disclosure ledger; use it to trace prompts and generated outputs, never as positive evidence of the team's academic language voice.

main_argument_chains.claim: Country medal forecasts can be built bottom-up from athlete or team histories and event-level allocation.
support_steps: Construct four cutoff-lagged capability features.
Fit separate medal and gold classifiers within each sport.
Transfer 2024 candidates and event assumptions to 2028.
Allocate event podium slots from fitted probabilities.
Aggregate event awards to NOC gold and total counts.
Repeat draws to form leading-country intervals.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper ranks USA, China, and Great Britain first and supplies point totals plus displayed intervals for nine NOCs.

main_argument_chains.claim: Nominal zero-medal countries can be ranked by simulated probability of receiving at least one 2028 medal.
support_steps: Label NOCs from athlete-file medal strings.
Reuse sport-level classifiers or fallbacks for candidate entrants.
Draw three distinct medalists per event.
Mark each candidate NOC appearing in a run.
Aggregate 500 runs into country probabilities and a count distribution.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Samoa, Mali, and Guam lead the reported ranking and the paper states an expected 4.78 new medal-winning NOCs, conditional on its cohort construction.

main_argument_chains.claim: Changes in sport event counts are associated differently with medal totals in USA swimming and China table tennis.
support_steps: Aggregate selected sport-country histories.
Fit a Poisson log-link model using NumEvents.
Interpret beta1 through an exponential ratio and a prediction curve.
Refit USA data under leave-one-year-out deletion.
Compare Poisson, Negative Binomial, and ZIP specifications.
Fit the analogous China table-tennis model and report its nonsignificant coefficient.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper recommends event expansion where the USA case appears positive but treats China's table-tennis dominance as comparatively stable.

main_argument_chains.claim: Host status, event opportunity, and recent medal history can be placed in one country-specific regression architecture.
support_steps: Define a host dummy.
Add event count as a program-size covariate.
Add the prior-three-Games medal mean as a history covariate.
Fit separate USA and China regressions.
Compare sample size, R-squared, host coefficient, and limitations.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper attributes larger medal increments to hosting for USA and China, while its own comparison table exposes limited sample and explanatory support.

main_argument_chains.claim: A coach-effect narrative can move from a component equation to a worked case and recipient-specific recommendations.
support_steps: Decompose observed capability into athlete, coach, and uncertainty terms.
Map podium outcomes to a 0-3 scale.
Use the previous three Games as the athlete baseline.
Set residual uncertainty to zero and difference current from baseline.
Apply the arithmetic to Lang Ping's USA and China tenures.
Name sports for India, Sweden, and Romania.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The technical branch is converted into an NOC investment recommendation format, although its causal and arithmetic claims remain bounded by the final warning pass.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper's communication architecture repeatedly converts model objects into scan-friendly paired outputs and diagnostics.
support_steps: Use task labels in the Summary.
Use a workflow diagram before equations.
Pair point bars with interval bars.
Place ROC, PR, and calibration together.
Pair the first-medal count histogram with sorted NOC probabilities.
Place LOO coefficients beside distribution-specification metrics.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Readers can follow task, model, result, and diagnostic handoffs without reconstructing the entire computational pipeline from prose alone.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: A compact workflow makes the official task decomposition visible.
Athlete photos and radar charts consume space and use mixed axes without explaining predictive relevance or uncertainty.
A sorted country bar chart communicates relative predicted medal counts but lacks intervals on the same view.
Gold and total interval bars show uncertainty for leading countries but not all requested results.
ROC, PR, and calibration curves expose discrimination and probability bias, but fold sample sizes and interval bands are absent.
Three correlation heatmaps are aligned and labeled, though they do not establish causal importance.
Accuracy and F1 bars summarize many sport models but obscure temporal leakage and target mismatch.
The histogram plus sorted probability bars is an appropriate pair for count and unit-level rare-event results.
A word cloud redundantly and imprecisely encodes the same probabilities and omits uncertainty.
LOO coefficients and side-by-side distribution metrics provide useful model-audit views despite invalid input grain.
